audit.whatIsWrong: The page's headline advice was "E his spin — the stun + dodge wins the trade", i.e. that Counter Strike dodges Judgment.
audit.why: Riot's text for Counter Strike is "dodge all incoming ATTACKS". Judgment is an ability, so its damage ticks straight through the dodge window; the value of E here is the stun on expiry, not damage negation. Cooldowns make it worse: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s while Judgment is 9/8.25/7.5/6.75/6s, so you never have an answer to every spin.
audit.corrected: Every "dodge his spin" line rewritten to "stun him out of the spin", with the 17s-vs-9s cooldown gap stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as a Jax spike off "Grandmaster's Might stats".
audit.why: Demacian Justice is flagged trueDamage and execute — it ignores the Armor and MR your own ultimate just gave you. Level 6 is Garen's spike, not yours, and Courage (22s at rank 1) is the other timer that decides whether your commit is worth anything.
audit.corrected: Level 6 rewritten as his spike with the true-damage reason, and real cooldowns written into the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart handed Jax Levels 1, 2 and 6 and called 3 and 4-5 Skill; the page also called a 45.72% matchup "Even" while diff said HARD.
audit.why: 45.72% over 3515 Emerald+ games, and every why-string on the page says Garen takes the early exchanges and owns level 6. The packet chart and the mirror both put Garen ahead through level 6 with Jax taking over at items.
audit.corrected: Rows 1 through 6 flipped to Garen in both layers as one atomic group with ratings moved down; first item and 2+ items stay Jax; difficulty raised to 7/10 and the final-rating line corrected to HARD.

edits.before: Still his window, and the danger jumps at 6. His W (Courage) gives a damage-reduction shield AND tenacity, so it eats the burst portion of your trade and shaves your Counter Strike stun shorter — even a clean E buys you less than it should. At 6 his R is a missing-HP TRUE-damage finisher: it goes straight through the Armor and MR your own Grandmaster at Arms just handed you, so staying above his execute window is your real defense. Don't all-in at low HP hoping your R resists save you; they don't against Demacian Justice. Hold E for his E-spin (it's the bulk of his damage and you can dodge it), never burn it on his Q.

Don't all-in at low HP hoping your R resists save you; they don't against Demacian Justice. Hold E for his E-spin — you never dodge Judgment's damage, only stun him out of it, and 17s against a 9s spin means one answer in two.

edits.before: This is where you take over. Garen's whole pattern is a Q-burst then a spin, and that loses to a duelist who can stick and stun the spin away. Once you hit two items, Counter Strike dodges his Judgment and stuns him out of it, Grandmaster at Arms' resists and on-hit ramp out-DPS him in any extended fight, and Leap Strike keeps you glued through his Q-silence disengage. Force him into a long 1v1 on the side lane where his front-loaded burst and R finisher aren't enough to close. Hold E for the spin, stun him through it, and the duel is yours.

notes: NAME CONFLICT the user should settle: the mirror (garen__jax) treats "Grandmaster-at-Arms" as the correct name for Jax's R and "Grandmaster's Might" as a fabrication; this page uses Grandmaster's Might in the full layer and Grandmaster at Arms in the content layer. Grandmaster at Arms is Jax's title and Grandmaster's Might is the ability, but champ-data/_kits/jax.json carries no ability names so neither is verifiable from the repo. I left the R name untouched on this page rather than fight the mirror — one ruling should be applied to every Jax matchup at once. Everything else here keys off the attacks-only wording of Counter Strike and the 17s-vs-9s cooldown gap against Judgment.
